tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

schema.name: SuggestSkills
schema.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

keywords.description: Topic keywords from the user's request.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 15 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem.

Usage:
- This tool will overwrite the existing file if there is one at the provided path.
- If this is an existing file, you MUST use the Read tool first to read the file's contents. This tool will fail if you did not read the file first.
- Prefer the Edit tool for modifying existing files — it only sends the diff. Only use this tool to create new files or for complete rewrites.
- NEVER create documentation files (*.md) or README files unless explicitly requested by the User.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid writing emojis to files unless asked.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

task_id.description: The task_id returned by the spawn_task call that created the chip.

reason.description: Optional one-line reason the suggestion is no longer needed, e.g. "fixed in this session" or "superseded by task_ab12cd34".

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

title.description: Under 60 chars. Imperative action phrase (start with a verb), e.g. "Fix stale README badge", "Remove dead config option". Shown as the chip label and the spawned session title.

prompt.description: The initial message for the spawned session. Self-contained — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation. Not shown directly in the UI.

tldr.description: One or two plain-English sentences shown on the suggestion card under the title. Lead with why you are suggesting this now — name what you noticed in this session — then say what the new session will do. Keep it readable: no file paths or code.

cwd.description: Optional. Absolute path to a different project root than the current session's — a path on the host this session runs on. The spawned session gets a fresh worktree under this path. Defaults to the current project — only set this when the work clearly belongs in another repo on that host.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. # Almanac implementation status

Updated 2026-09-13. Work continues from `8836166` on `codex/manual-entry`; all
preceding commits are preserved. The nutrition work below is uncommitted in the
working tree. Nothing pushed.

## Verified core

Swift 6.3.3 on x86_64 Linux (`yamal`, `source env.sh`): **115 XCTest tests —
114 pass, 1 opt-in test skipped, zero failures.** Plain `swift build && swift
test`; the default parallel build works on this machine. The skipped test
imports the real bundle, and passes when enabled:

```sh
ALMANAC_NUTRITION_BUNDLE=~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite \
    swift test --filter NutritionRealBundleTests
```

Python 3.14, `tools/nutrition`: **101 unittest tests, zero failures**, including
the real-lake integration tests:

```sh
cd tools/nutrition && ALMANAC_NUTRITION_INTEGRATION=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```

Earlier records: 85 tests on Swift 6.0.3 in the 2026-09-08 session container
(`-j 1 -Xswiftc -disable-batch-mode`); 79 on Swift 6.3.3 per the user log. No
change has been run on an Apple platform.

## Nutrition module (2026-09-13)

The 2026-09-13 handoff's build order, steps 1–6:

1. Nutrient dictionary and qualifier vocabulary as data: `tools/nutrition/dictionary/`.
2. USDA Foundation Foods extracted, and 3. canonicalised (395 foods).
4. Bundle step with the failing licence assertion (`A`, `B`, `N` or the build
   fails), built while USDA was the only source.
5. CIQUAL 2025, CoFID 2021 and AFCD R3 extracted and canonicalised; union; the
   bundle holds 8,354 foods and 49,036 values. `qa` re-reads every mapped raw
   cell with independent readers: passed, 0 tokens coerced.
6. AlmanacCore: `LicenceGroup.native` (`N`, ships; the `almanac` namespace moved
   from `A` to `N`); `NutrientValue.basis`; migration 008 (`nutrition_*`
   reference tables with licence and qualifier CHECKs);
   `NutritionReferenceImporter` (re-runs the licence assertion against Swift's
   own registry before copying anything, in one transaction); `NutritionCatalog`
   (food, values, bases, calories, folded search); `GeneralAtwater` and
   `EnergyEstimate` (4/4/9/7 on total carbohydrate, publisher's figure as a
   labelled fallback).

# Nutrition — calorie reference database, v1

**Status:** built 2026-09-13. Reference data and calorie calculation only; no
food logging, portions or UI yet.
**Decisions it implements:** the 2026-09-13 handoff (licence group N; general
Atwater 4/4/9/7; calorie-only canonical set; Branded Foods held out; SFDA never
stored) and Processing Design v0.1 in the food-data lake.

---

## 1. What exists

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Pipeline: extract → canonicalise → union → bundle → qa | `tools/nutrition/` (Python; `README.md` there is the contract) |
| Nutrient dictionary, qualifiers, licence groups, sources — as data | `tools/nutrition/dictionary/*.csv` |
| Bundle (what ships) | `~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite`, schema version 1 |
| Reference tables | `Migration008_NutritionReference` (`nutrition_*`) |
| Bundle import, with the licence assertion run again | `NutritionReferenceImporter` |
| Read seam: food, values, bases, calories, search | `NutritionCatalog` |
| Calorie calculation | `GeneralAtwater`, `EnergyEstimate` |

The bundle holds 8,354 foods and 49,036 values from four sources:

| Source | Namespace | Group | Foods | Values |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| USDA FoodData Central 2026-04-30, Foundation Foods | `usda` | A | 395 | 1,867 |
| ANSES-CIQUAL 2025 | `ciqual` | B | 3,484 | 20,904 |
| CoFID 2021 | `cofid` | B | 2,887 | 15,459 |
| AFCD Release 3 | `afcd` | B | 1,588 | 10,806 |
| Almanac-native | `almanac` | N | 0 — awaiting dish data | |

## 2. The value

Every value is the §2 value model plus a basis: amount, qualifier, the source's
own confidence or derivation marker, the original cell text, the source's
nutrient id and unit, licence group, and `per_100g` or `per_100ml`.

- **A token never becomes a number.** CoFID `Tr` and CIQUAL `traces` are
  `trace`; CoFID `N` and CIQUAL `-` are `not_analysed`; both keep an empty
  amount and their original text. The pipeline refuses such a row with an
  amount, the bundle's and the device's tables refuse it (`CHECK`), and QA
  re-reads every raw cell to prove it.
- **A blank cell is no row.** "The source says nothing" and "the source says it
  has no number" are different facts, and both survive.
- **A 0 is only ever a published 0** (`zero_reported`).
- **A negative published amount is not a quantity** — no row, recorded in the
  source's manifest, never clamped to 0.
- **Per 100 g and per 100 mL never mix.** CoFID alcoholic beverages and AFCD's
  213 liquids carry `per_100ml`; AFCD liquids have both bases.

## 3. Identity

A reference food is the publisher's identifier in its namespace —
`usda:2346403`, `ciqual:1000`, `cofid:13-145`, `afcd:F002258` — never a
surrogate, because a food log must keep pointing at the same food across bundle
updates. When a publisher reuses an identifier within one release, every
occurrence becomes `{id}@row{n}` (CoFID 2021 uses `13-669` for two foods).

## 4. Licence enforcement, in four places

1. **Pipeline bundle step** — every row's group must be shippable (A, B, N) and
   agree with `dictionary/sources.csv`, or the build fails before any output
   exists.
2. **The bundle file** — its tables carry `CHECK (licence_group IN ('A','B','N'))`.
3. **Device import** — `NutritionReferenceImporter` re-runs `BundleGuard` over
   every source, food and value row and checks each group against
   `SourceIdentifier.Namespace.licenceGroup`. A restricted row throws
   `LicenceViolation` naming the row; a shippable group that disagrees with its
   namespace throws too. Nothing is written unless everything passes.
4. **Device tables** — migration 008 repeats the `CHECK`s, so no route inserts a
   restricted row.

A Swift test reads `tools/nutrition/dictionary/` and fails if the pipeline and
AlmanacCore ever disagree about qualifiers, licence groups or a source's group.

## 5. Calories

Almanac's calorie number is **general Atwater**: 4 kcal/g protein, 4 kcal/g
total carbohydrate, 9 kcal/g fat, 7 kcal/g alcohol — computed in AlmanacCore,
never stored, so native entries and reference foods share one implementation.

General Atwater assumes *total* carbohydrate (by difference, fibre included).
The term is chosen per food:

| Published | Carbohydrate term | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| Carbohydrate by difference | as published | USDA |
| Available carbohydrate + dietary fibre | sum | CIQUAL, AFCD |
| Available carbohydrate as monosaccharide equivalents + fibre | sum | CoFID |

Fibre is never assumed: available carbohydrate without a fibre value gives no
total. A trace or a "< x" enters the sum as 0, and so does absent or unanalysed
alcohol; `EnergyEstimate.inputsTakenAsZero` names every such input. When general
Atwater cannot be computed, `EnergyEstimate.preferred` falls back to the
publisher's own energy, marked `publisherReported`. It never shows a trace, an
unanalysed value or a bound as a calorie figure.

Coverage on the current bundle (food–basis pairs):

| Source | General Atwater | Publisher's figure | Neither |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| USDA | 312 | 8 | 48 |
| CIQUAL | 3,367 | 31 | 86 |
| CoFID | 1,533 | 1,318 | 36 |
| AFCD | 1,801 | 0 | 0 |

CoFID leaves AOAC fibre blank for 46 % of its foods, hence its fallback share.
Against USDA's own published general-Atwater figure, Almanac's differs by a
median of 0.0 kcal over 311 foods. The largest differences from publishers'
own figures are high-fibre and sugar-free foods, where general factors count
fibre and polyols at 4 kcal/g; per-food factors are the decided v2 refinement.

## 6. Search

`NutritionCatalog.search` matches any language's name, folded with Laboratory's
`TextFold` (case, accents, Arabic letter variants), each food once, ordered by
primary name. Names are folded once, at import.

## 7. Not done

- **Almanac-native foods** — the pipeline slot and group N exist; the Saudi/Gulf
  dish data does not.
- **App wiring** — the app target must ship `almanac.sqlite` as a resource and
  call `importBundle(at:)` on first launch and after an update. Not done here:
  no Apple toolchain in this environment.
- **Food logging, portions and household measures** (USDA `food_portion`, CoFID
  specific gravity), SR Legacy, FNDDS, Branded Foods, Frida, Oman FCT 2024.
- **Per-food Atwater factors** (v2).

1	import Foundation

3	// MARK: - Values
4	
5	public enum NutritionError: Error, CustomStringConvertible, Sendable {
6	    case foodNotFound(SourceIdentifier)
7	    case invalidGramWeight(Double)
8	    case invalidAmount(Double)
9	    case notANativeFood(SourceIdentifier)
10	    case recipeCycle(SourceIdentifier)
11	    case notARemovableSource(SourceIdentifier.Namespace)
12	    case dishHasNoRecipe(SourceIdentifier)
13	
14	    public var description: String {
15	        switch self {
16	        case .foodNotFound(let ref):
17	            return "no food '\(ref)' in the nutrition catalog."
18	        case .invalidGramWeight(let g):
19	            return "a portion's gram weight must be finite and greater than zero; got \(g)."
20	        case .invalidAmount(let a):
21	            return "a measure's amount must be finite and greater than zero; got \(a)."
22	        case .notANativeFood(let ref):
23	            return "'\(ref)' is published by \(ref.namespace.rawValue); only 'almanac:' foods "
24	                 + "may be authored here. A publisher's row is corrected upstream, not edited."
25	        case .recipeCycle(let ref):
26	            return "'\(ref)' would end up an ingredient of itself, directly or through "
27	                 + "another dish. The reduction would then compute each from the other's "
28	                 + "previous answer and report a number with nothing behind it."
29	        case .dishHasNoRecipe(let ref):
30	            return "'\(ref)' has no recipe to recompute from. Its values were entered "
31	                 + "directly, and reducing an empty ingredient list would replace them "
32	                 + "with nothing."
33	        case .notARemovableSource(let namespace):
34	            return "'\(namespace.rawValue)' is Almanac's own namespace. Removing a source is "
35	                 + "for a publisher withdrawing its data; it is not a way to delete the "
36	                 + "dishes a person wrote."
37	        }

144	        INSERT INTO nutrition_food

146	             yield_grams, source_value, created_at, updated_at)
147	        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)

149	            name_text         = excluded.name_text,
150	            name_fold         = excluded.name_fold,
151	            licence_group     = excluded.licence_group,
152	            edible_proportion = excluded.edible_proportion,
153	            yield_grams       = excluded.yield_grams,
154	            source_value      = excluded.source_value,
155	            updated_at        = excluded.updated_at;
156	        """, [
157	            .text(food.ref.description), .text(food.nameText),
158	            .text(TextFold.fold(food.nameText)), .text(food.licenceGroup.rawValue),
159	            food.edibleProportion.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
160	            food.yieldGrams.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
161	            food.sourceValue.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,

167	    public func food(_ ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> NutritionFood? {
168	        try db.query("""
169	            SELECT food_ref, name_text, licence_group, edible_proportion, yield_grams, source_value
170	            FROM nutrition_food WHERE food_ref = ?;
171	            """, [.text(ref.description)]).first.flatMap(NutritionCatalog.food(from:))
172	    }

174	    /// Name search, folded across case, diacritics and script by `TextFold` —
175	    /// the same folding Laboratory's alias lookup uses, so "بصل" and "Basal"
176	    /// behave the same way here as there.
177	    public func search(_ text: String, limit: Int = 20) throws -> [NutritionFood] {
178	        let fold = TextFold.fold(text)
179	        guard !fold.isEmpty else { return [] }
180	        return try db.query("""
181	            SELECT food_ref, name_text, licence_group, edible_proportion, yield_grams, source_value
182	            FROM nutrition_food WHERE name_fold LIKE ? ESCAPE '\\'
183	            ORDER BY LENGTH(name_fold), name_fold LIMIT ?;
184	            """, [.text("%\(NutritionCatalog.escapingWildcards(fold))%"),
185	                  .integer(Int64(limit))])
186	            .compactMap(NutritionCatalog.food(from:))
187	    }

189	    /// `%` and `_` in a search term are characters the user typed, not wildcards.
190	    static func escapingWildcards(_ text: String) -> String {
191	        text.replacingOccurrences(of: "\\", with: "\\\\")
192	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "%", with: "\\%")
193	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "_", with: "\\_")
194	    }

199	              let group = row.string("licence_group").flatMap(LicenceGroup.init(rawValue:))
200	        else { return nil }
201	        return NutritionFood(ref: ref, nameText: name, licenceGroup: group,
202	                             edibleProportion: row.double("edible_proportion"),
203	                             yieldGrams: row.double("yield_grams"),
204	                             sourceValue: row.string("source_value"))
205	    }

207	    /// Removes every row a publisher contributed: its foods, their values and
208	    /// their portions.
209	    ///
210	    /// `SourceIdentifier` namespaces exist so that this is one delete when a
211	    /// rights holder says no. Until now that was a claim in a comment with no
212	    /// code behind it. Returns how many foods went.
213	    ///
214	    /// What deliberately survives: the user's food log entries, which keep the
215	    /// name they were logged under and are reported by `NutritionTotals` as
216	    /// `mealsWithoutReference`; and any `almanac:` dish built on the removed
217	    /// rows, whose recipe is kept and whose reduction now reports
218	    /// `missingComponents`. A withdrawal by a publisher is a fact about the
219	    /// publisher, not permission to erase what the person recorded eating.
220	    @discardableResult
221	    public func removeSource(_ namespace: SourceIdentifier.Namespace) throws -> Int {
222	        // Almanac's own rows are not a third party's to withdraw, and this call
223	        // would silently delete every dish the person wrote.
224	        guard namespace != .almanac else {
225	            throw NutritionError.notARemovableSource(namespace)
226	        }
227	        // Safe as a LIKE pattern because Namespace is a closed enum and no raw
228	        // value contains `%` or `_`. A namespace that did would need escaping,
229	        // as `search` does for text a person typed.
230	        return try db.run("DELETE FROM nutrition_food WHERE food_ref LIKE ?;",
231	                          [.text("\(namespace.rawValue):%")])
232	    }

302	    public func addPortion(_ portion: NutritionPortion) throws -> String {
303	        guard portion.gramWeight.isFinite, portion.gramWeight > 0 else {

314	        // Re-importing a measure already held updates it rather than storing a
315	        // second copy — two identical rows would otherwise read as an ambiguity
316	        // between a row and itself. See Migration009.
317	        try db.run("""
318	        INSERT INTO nutrition_portion
319	            (id, food_ref, amount, unit_text, unit_fold, modifier_text,
320	             gram_weight, sequence, licence_group, source_value)
321	        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
322	        ON CONFLICT(food_ref, unit_fold, COALESCE(modifier_text, ''), amount, gram_weight)
323	        DO UPDATE SET
324	            unit_text     = excluded.unit_text,
325	            sequence      = excluded.sequence,
326	            licence_group = excluded.licence_group,
327	            source_value  = excluded.source_value;
328	        """, [
329	            .text(portion.id), .text(portion.foodRef.description), .real(portion.amount),
330	            .text(portion.unitText), .text(TextFold.fold(portion.unitText)),
331	            portion.modifierText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
332	            .real(portion.gramWeight), .integer(Int64(portion.sequence)),
333	            .text(portion.licenceGroup.rawValue),
334	            portion.sourceValue.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null
335	        ])
336	        // The held row's id, which is the caller's only when this was an insert.
337	        return try db.query("""
338	            SELECT id FROM nutrition_portion
339	            WHERE food_ref = ? AND unit_fold = ? AND COALESCE(modifier_text, '') = ?
340	              AND amount = ? AND gram_weight = ?;
341	            """, [.text(portion.foodRef.description), .text(TextFold.fold(portion.unitText)),
342	                  .text(portion.modifierText ?? ""), .real(portion.amount),

347	    public func portions(of ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> [NutritionPortion] {
348	        try db.query("""
349	            SELECT id, food_ref, amount, unit_text, modifier_text, gram_weight,
350	                   sequence, licence_group, source_value
351	            FROM nutrition_portion WHERE food_ref = ? ORDER BY sequence, unit_text;
352	            """, [.text(ref.description)]).compactMap(NutritionCatalog.portion(from:))

355	    /// What one named measure of this food weighs.
356	    ///
357	    /// A `modifier` narrows the search — "1 cup, cooked" against "1 cup, raw".
358	    /// When several rows still match, they all come back: choosing between two
359	    /// gram weights is the caller's decision with the user in front of it, not
360	    /// a silent pick by row order.
361	    public func portion(of ref: SourceIdentifier, unit: String,
362	                        modifier: String? = nil) throws -> PortionMatch {
363	        let forms = NutritionCatalog.matchableForms(unit)
364	        guard !forms.isEmpty else { return .notFound }
365	        var candidates = try db.query("""
366	            SELECT id, food_ref, amount, unit_text, modifier_text, gram_weight,
367	                   sequence, licence_group, source_value
368	            FROM nutrition_portion
369	            WHERE food_ref = ? AND unit_fold IN (?, ?, ?)
370	            ORDER BY sequence, id;
371	            """, [.text(ref.description), .text(forms[0]), .text(forms[1]), .text(forms[2])])
372	            .compactMap(NutritionCatalog.portion(from:))
373	
374	        if let modifier {
375	            let wanted = TextFold.fold(modifier)
376	            let narrowed = candidates.filter {
377	                TextFold.fold($0.modifierText ?? "") == wanted
378	            }
379	            // An unmatched modifier narrows to nothing rather than falling back
380	            // to every row: "1 cup, cooked" must not quietly answer with raw.
381	            candidates = narrowed
382	        }
383	
384	        switch candidates.count {
385	        case 0:  return .notFound
386	        case 1:  return .one(candidates[0])
387	        default: return .ambiguous(candidates)
388	        }
389	    }
390	
391	    /// Resolves a household measure to grams — "2 cups" → 316 g.
392	    ///
393	    /// Nil when the measure is unknown or ambiguous. The caller stores the
394	    /// number; it is deliberately not recomputed at read time, because a later
395	    /// correction to a gram weight must not silently change the mass of a meal
396	    /// the user already confirmed.
397	    public func grams(of ref: SourceIdentifier, amount: Double, unit: String,
398	                      modifier: String? = nil) throws -> Double? {
399	        guard amount.isFinite, amount > 0 else { throw NutritionError.invalidAmount(amount) }
400	        guard let portion = try self.portion(of: ref, unit: unit, modifier: modifier).resolved
401	        else { return nil }
402	        return portion.gramsPerUnit * amount
403	    }
404	
405	    /// The edible weight of an as-purchased weight — a banana with its skin.
406	    ///
407	    /// Nil where the source stated no edible proportion. Returning the input
408	    /// unchanged would assert that all of it is edible, which is exactly the
409	    /// claim a missing factor does not make.
410	    public func edibleGrams(of ref: SourceIdentifier, asPurchased grams: Double) throws -> Double? {
411	        guard let proportion = try food(ref)?.edibleProportion else { return nil }
412	        return grams * proportion
413	    }
414	
415	    /// The folded forms a typed measure may match: itself, its plural, and its
416	    /// singular. Always three, so the query shape is fixed.
417	    ///
418	    /// `TextFold` normalises case, diacritics and script — not grammar — so a
419	    /// stored "cup" never matched a typed "cups", and "2 cups" is exactly the
420	    /// input this feature exists to answer. Matching extra forms at *query*
421	    /// time rather than normalising what is stored means nothing is lost on
422	    /// the way in and two genuinely different units are never merged: a
423	    /// publisher shipping both "cup" and "cups" rows still comes back
424	    /// `.ambiguous`, which is the honest answer.
425	    ///
426	    /// ponytail: English -s only. "glasses"/"glass" and other -es plurals miss
427	    /// and fall out as `.notFound`, which the caller already handles. A unit
428	    /// dictionary is the upgrade if a source ships measures this gets wrong.
429	    static func matchableForms(_ unit: String) -> [String] {
430	        let fold = TextFold.fold(unit)
431	        guard !fold.isEmpty else { return [] }
432	        let singular = fold.count > 2 && fold.hasSuffix("s") ? String(fold.dropLast()) : fold
433	        return [fold, fold + "s", singular]
434	    }
435	
436	    private static func portion(from row: Row) -> NutritionPortion? {
437	        guard let id = row.string("id"),
438	              let ref = row.string("food_ref").flatMap(SourceIdentifier.init(parsing:)),
439	              let amount = row.double("amount"), let unit = row.string("unit_text"),
440	              let gramWeight = row.double("gram_weight"),
441	              let group = row.string("licence_group").flatMap(LicenceGroup.init(rawValue:))
442	        else { return nil }
443	        return NutritionPortion(
444	            foodRef: ref, amount: amount, unitText: unit, gramWeight: gramWeight,
445	            modifierText: row.string("modifier_text"),
446	            sequence: Int(row.int("sequence") ?? 0), licenceGroup: group,
447	            sourceValue: row.string("source_value"), id: id)
448	    }
449	}

3	/// Canonical nutrient ids this module reasons about by name.
4	///
5	/// Deliberately not the whole nutrient dictionary. These are the six the energy
6	/// calculation and the dish reduction need to *name*; every other nutrient
7	/// travels as an opaque id and is summed without being understood, which is all
8	/// a total requires.
9	public enum Nutrient {
10	    public static let protein = "protein"
11	    public static let fat = "fat"
12	    public static let carbohydrate = "carbohydrate"
13	    public static let alcohol = "alcohol"
14	    public static let fibre = "fibre"
15	    /// What the publisher reported, in kcal. Never overwritten with a computed
16	    /// figure — the two are different claims and `EnergyEstimate.basis` says
17	    /// which one a number came from.
18	    public static let energyKcal = "energy_kcal"
19	}
20	
21	/// The general Atwater factors: 4/4/9/7 kcal per gram.
22	///
23	/// Used in preference to each publisher's own specific factors, and the reason
24	/// is comparability rather than accuracy. A day's log can mix USDA, CIQUAL,
25	/// CoFID and AFCD rows; those four apply different factor systems, so summing
26	/// their reported energies adds numbers that were not computed the same way.
27	/// Recomputing every food through one factor set makes the day's total mean
28	/// something. Where the macros are missing, `EnergyEstimate` falls back to what
29	/// the publisher reported and says so rather than returning a smaller number.
30	public enum GeneralAtwater {
31	    public static let proteinKcalPerGram = 4.0
32	    public static let carbohydrateKcalPerGram = 4.0
33	    public static let fatKcalPerGram = 9.0
34	    public static let alcoholKcalPerGram = 7.0
35	
36	    public static func kcal(protein: Double, fat: Double,
37	                            carbohydrate: Double, alcohol: Double = 0) -> Double {
38	        protein * proteinKcalPerGram
39	            + fat * fatKcalPerGram
40	            + carbohydrate * carbohydrateKcalPerGram
41	            + alcohol * alcoholKcalPerGram
42	    }
43	}

45	public struct EnergyEstimate: Sendable, Hashable {
46	    public let kcal: Double
47	    public let basis: Basis
48	
49	    public enum Basis: String, Sendable, Hashable, Codable {
50	        /// Computed from the macronutrients with the general factors.
51	        case generalAtwater = "general_atwater"
52	        /// The publisher's own energy figure, used because the macros needed
53	        /// to compute one were not analysed.
54	        case publisherReported = "publisher_reported"
55	    }
56	
57	    public init(kcal: Double, basis: Basis) {
58	        self.kcal = kcal
59	        self.basis = basis
60	    }
61	
62	    /// Energy per 100 g of edible portion, from that food's stored values.
63	    ///
64	    /// Nil when neither route is available — which is a different answer from
65	    /// zero, and the only honest one for a food nobody has analysed.
66	    public static func per100g(_ values: [NutrientValue]) -> EnergyEstimate? {
67	        func usable(_ id: String) -> Double? {
68	            guard let value = values.first(where: { $0.nutrientID == id }) else { return nil }
69	            switch value.qualifier {
70	            // Present but below the limit of quantification. Counting it as its
71	            // reported number would overstate; dropping the food would
72	            // understate. Zero is what "below the smallest measurable amount"
73	            // contributes to a day's energy.
74	            case .trace, .belowLOQ: return 0
75	            // Nobody measured it. Not zero, and not something to guess.
76	            case .notAnalysed: return nil
77	            default: return value.amount
78	            }
79	        }
80	
81	        if let protein = usable(Nutrient.protein), let fat = usable(Nutrient.fat),
82	           let carbohydrate = usable(Nutrient.carbohydrate) {
83	            // A food with no alcohol row is taken as containing none. Every
84	            // composition database in groups A and B reports alcohol for the
85	            // items that carry it, so the absent case is "not an alcoholic
86	            // food" rather than "unmeasured".
87	            return EnergyEstimate(
88	                kcal: GeneralAtwater.kcal(protein: protein, fat: fat,
89	                                          carbohydrate: carbohydrate,
90	                                          alcohol: usable(Nutrient.alcohol) ?? 0),
91	                basis: .generalAtwater)
92	        }
93	        if let reported = usable(Nutrient.energyKcal) {
94	            return EnergyEstimate(kcal: reported, basis: .publisherReported)
95	        }
96	        return nil
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Scales a per-100 g estimate to an actual mass.
100	    public func scaled(toGrams grams: Double) -> EnergyEstimate {
101	        EnergyEstimate(kcal: kcal * grams / 100, basis: basis)
102	    }
103	}

109	    /// `belowLOQ` scale to zero and keep their qualifier, so a total can still
110	    /// report that the food contributed something too small to count.

112	        switch qualifier {
113	        case .notAnalysed: return nil
114	        case .trace, .belowLOQ: return 0
115	        default: return amount.map { $0 * grams / 100 }
116	        }
117	    }

8	/// "the user ate 150 g of it". That is this table.
9	///
10	/// Two decisions worth the words:
11	///
12	/// 1. **`food_ref` is text, with no foreign key.** It holds a
13	///    `SourceIdentifier` — `usda:1105904`, `almanac:dish-kabsa`. Processing
14	///    Design v0.1 §3 keeps "remove a whole source" a one-line delete when a
15	///    rights holder says no; a foreign key with ON DELETE CASCADE would turn
16	///    that delete into the erasure of the user's own meal history. The log is
17	///    the user's record, not the publisher's, and it outlives the reference
18	///    rows it points at. `food_name_text` is what keeps an orphaned row
19	///    readable — the same reversibility discipline as
20	///    `NutrientValue.sourceValue` and `lab_observation.source_analyte_text`.
21	/// 2. **`grams` is nullable.** "Some rice, amount not stated" is a thing a
22	///    person logs, and NutrientQualifier already establishes that this
23	///    codebase does not write a number where nobody supplied one. An entry
24	///    with no amount yields no energy and says so, rather than yielding zero.
25	///

27	/// reference values and the grams, and storing it would freeze one answer to
28	/// a question whose inputs get corrected.

31	    public static let name = "nutrition_log"

35	        CREATE TABLE nutrition_log (

63	/// Authoring for Almanac's own foods — the `almanac:` namespace, and only it.
64	///
65	/// A dish is reference data, not a record of the user's body, so it carries no
66	/// revision history: `lab_catalog_analyte` is upserted the same way for the
67	/// same reason, while `lab_observation` and `nutrition_log` — which *are*
68	/// records about a person — are revision-tracked. Adding dish revisions later
69	/// is an additive migration, not a redesign.
70	///
71	/// A publisher's row is never editable here. Correcting `usda:1105904` is
72	/// something USDA does; pretending otherwise would put an Almanac edit behind a
73	/// publisher's identifier and make the next import silently overwrite it.
74	public struct NutritionDishEditor: Sendable {
75	    private let db: Database
76	    private let clock: any Clock
77	    private let catalog: NutritionCatalog
78	
79	    public init(db: Database, clock: any Clock = SystemClock()) {
80	        self.db = db
81	        self.clock = clock
82	        self.catalog = NutritionCatalog(db: db, clock: clock)
83	    }
84	
85	    private static func requireNative(_ ref: SourceIdentifier) throws {
86	        guard ref.namespace == .almanac else { throw NutritionError.notANativeFood(ref) }
87	    }
88	
89	    // MARK: Creating and editing the dish itself
90	
91	    @discardableResult
92	    public func create(localID: String, nameText: String,
93	                       yieldGrams: Double? = nil,
94	                       edibleProportion: Double? = nil) throws -> SourceIdentifier {
95	        let ref = SourceIdentifier(namespace: .almanac, localID: localID)
96	        try catalog.upsert(NutritionFood(
97	            ref: ref, nameText: nameText, licenceGroup: ref.namespace.licenceGroup,
98	            edibleProportion: edibleProportion, yieldGrams: yieldGrams,
99	            sourceValue: nil))
100	        return ref
101	    }
102	
103	    /// Per-100 g values typed in directly — a package label, or a figure the
104	    /// person knows. The alternative route is `setRecipe`.
105	    public func setValues(_ values: [NutrientValue], for ref: SourceIdentifier) throws {
106	        try NutritionDishEditor.requireNative(ref)
107	        try catalog.setValues(values, for: ref)
108	    }
109	
110	    /// Applies a correction. Returns false when the edit changed nothing.
111	    ///
112	    /// A changed yield re-reduces the recipe, because the stored per-100 g
113	    /// values are per 100 g *of the finished dish* — leaving them alone would
114	    /// keep numbers that no longer describe anything.
115	    @discardableResult
116	    public func update(_ ref: SourceIdentifier, _ edit: DishEdit) throws -> Bool {
117	        try NutritionDishEditor.requireNative(ref)
118	        guard let held = try catalog.food(ref) else { throw NutritionError.foodNotFound(ref) }
119	        guard edit.touchesAnything else { return false }
120	
121	        // A dish must be called something, so `.clear` on the name is a no-op
122	        // rather than an error case nobody would ever hit deliberately.
123	        let name = edit.nameText.resolve(held.nameText, cleared: held.nameText)
124	        let yield = edit.yieldGrams.resolve(held.yieldGrams)
125	        let edible = edit.edibleProportion.resolve(held.edibleProportion)
126	        guard name != held.nameText || yield != held.yieldGrams
127	                || edible != held.edibleProportion else { return false }
128	
129	        try catalog.upsert(NutritionFood(
130	            ref: ref, nameText: name, licenceGroup: held.licenceGroup,
131	            edibleProportion: edible, yieldGrams: yield, sourceValue: held.sourceValue))
132	        if yield != held.yieldGrams, try !components(of: ref).isEmpty {
133	            _ = try reduceAndStore(ref)
134	        }
135	        return true
136	    }
137	
138	    /// Removes the dish, its values and its components. A food log entry that
139	    /// pointed at it keeps its own row and its logged name — the log holds no
140	    /// foreign key here, exactly so that this delete cannot reach it.
141	    @discardableResult
142	    public func delete(_ ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> Bool {
143	        try NutritionDishEditor.requireNative(ref)
144	        return try db.run("DELETE FROM nutrition_food WHERE food_ref = ?;",
145	                          [.text(ref.description)]) == 1
146	    }

148	    public func dishes() throws -> [NutritionFood] {
149	        try db.query("""
150	            SELECT food_ref, name_text, licence_group, edible_proportion, yield_grams, source_value
151	            FROM nutrition_food WHERE food_ref LIKE 'almanac:%' ORDER BY name_fold;
152	            """).compactMap(NutritionCatalog.food(from:))
153	    }
154	
155	    // MARK: The recipe
156	
157	    public func components(of ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> [DishComponent] {
158	        try db.query("""
159	            SELECT component_ref, grams, note_text FROM nutrition_dish_component
160	            WHERE dish_ref = ? ORDER BY sequence;
161	            """, [.text(ref.description)]).compactMap { row in
162	            guard let componentRef = row.string("component_ref")
163	                    .flatMap(SourceIdentifier.init(parsing:)),
164	                  let grams = row.double("grams") else { return nil }
165	            return DishComponent(componentRef, grams: grams, noteText: row.string("note_text"))
166	        }
167	    }
168	
169	    /// Replaces the recipe and recomputes the dish's per-100 g values from it.
170	    @discardableResult
171	    public func setRecipe(_ components: [DishComponent], for ref: SourceIdentifier,
172	                          yieldGrams: Double? = nil) throws -> RecipeReduction {
173	        try NutritionDishEditor.requireNative(ref)
174	        guard let held = try catalog.food(ref) else { throw NutritionError.foodNotFound(ref) }
175	        for component in components {
176	            guard component.grams.isFinite, component.grams > 0 else {
177	                throw NutritionError.invalidGramWeight(component.grams)
178	            }
179	            guard try !recipeReaches(ref, from: component.ref) else {
180	                throw NutritionError.recipeCycle(ref)
181	            }
182	        }
183	
184	        // One transaction over all three writes. A recipe stored with the
185	        // values of the recipe before it is a dish whose numbers describe
186	        // nothing, and that is exactly what a failure between these steps used
187	        // to leave behind.
188	        return try db.transaction { () throws -> RecipeReduction in
189	            try db.run("DELETE FROM nutrition_dish_component WHERE dish_ref = ?;",
190	                       [.text(ref.description)])
191	            for (index, component) in components.enumerated() {
192	                try db.run("""
193	                INSERT INTO nutrition_dish_component
194	                    (id, dish_ref, component_ref, grams, sequence, note_text)
195	                VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
196	                """, [
197	                    .text(UUID().uuidString), .text(ref.description),
198	                    .text(component.ref.description), .real(component.grams),
199	                    .integer(Int64(index)),
200	                    component.noteText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null
201	                ])
202	            }
203	            if let yieldGrams, yieldGrams != held.yieldGrams {
204	                // Written directly rather than through `update`, whose own
205	                // recompute would then run against the recipe twice.
206	                try catalog.upsert(NutritionFood(
207	                    ref: ref, nameText: held.nameText, licenceGroup: held.licenceGroup,
208	                    edibleProportion: held.edibleProportion, yieldGrams: yieldGrams,
209	                    sourceValue: held.sourceValue))
210	            }
211	            // Not `recompute`: emptying a recipe deliberately is allowed to
212	            // empty the values with it, which `recompute` refuses to do.
213	            return try reduceAndStore(ref)
214	        }
215	    }
216	
217	    /// Whether `dish` already appears anywhere under `start`'s recipe.
218	    ///
219	    /// A dish may be an ingredient of another dish — that is the point of
220	    /// reducing to per-100 g values — but a loop is not stale data, it is two
221	    /// dishes each computed from the other's previous answer, and the reduction
222	    /// terminates on stored values so it would produce that number in silence.
223	    /// Walks the graph with a visited set rather than a depth limit, so a cycle
224	    /// already in the data cannot hang this.
225	    private func recipeReaches(_ dish: SourceIdentifier,
226	                               from start: SourceIdentifier) throws -> Bool {
227	        var queue = [start]
228	        var seen: Set<SourceIdentifier> = []
229	        while let next = queue.popLast() {
230	            guard seen.insert(next).inserted else { continue }
231	            if next == dish { return true }
232	            // Only Almanac's own foods have recipes; a publisher's row is a leaf.
233	            guard next.namespace == .almanac else { continue }
234	            queue.append(contentsOf: try components(of: next).map(\.ref))
235	        }
236	        return false
237	    }
238	
239	    /// Re-reduces the stored recipe and writes the result.
240	    ///
241	    /// Explicit rather than automatic on read: a dish's values are stored so a
242	    /// day's total is one query, and recomputing them on every read would make
243	    /// a correction to an ingredient silently rewrite history instead of being
244	    /// an action someone took.
245	    @discardableResult
246	    public func recompute(_ ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> RecipeReduction {
247	        try NutritionDishEditor.requireNative(ref)
248	        // A dish whose per-100 g values were typed in has nothing to reduce
249	        // from, and reducing an empty ingredient list yields an empty result —
250	        // so this would have quietly replaced what the person entered with
251	        // nothing. Refusing is the only answer that does not lose data.
252	        guard try !components(of: ref).isEmpty else {
253	            throw NutritionError.dishHasNoRecipe(ref)
254	        }
255	        return try reduceAndStore(ref)
256	    }
257	
258	    /// The reduction and the write, with no guard. `recompute` is the public
259	    /// door and carries the guard; `setRecipe` comes in here because emptying a
260	    /// recipe on purpose is allowed to empty the values with it.
261	    @discardableResult
262	    private func reduceAndStore(_ ref: SourceIdentifier) throws -> RecipeReduction {
263	        guard let held = try catalog.food(ref) else { throw NutritionError.foodNotFound(ref) }
264	        let reduction = try reduce(try components(of: ref), yieldGrams: held.yieldGrams, as: ref)
265	        try catalog.setValues(reduction.values, for: ref)
266	        return reduction
267	    }
268	
269	    /// The reduction itself, with no writing. Exposed so a person can see what
270	    /// a recipe comes to before committing it.
271	    public func reduce(_ components: [DishComponent], yieldGrams: Double? = nil,
272	                       as ref: SourceIdentifier = SourceIdentifier(namespace: .almanac,
273	                                                                   localID: "unsaved-recipe")
274	    ) throws -> RecipeReduction {
275	        let componentGrams = components.reduce(0) { $0 + $1.grams }
276	        let totalGrams = yieldGrams ?? componentGrams
277	
278	        var missing: [SourceIdentifier] = []
279	        var loaded: [(component: DishComponent, values: [NutrientValue])] = []
280	        for component in components {
281	            guard try catalog.food(component.ref) != nil else {
282	                missing.append(component.ref)
283	                continue
284	            }
285	            loaded.append((component, try catalog.values(of: component.ref)))
286	        }
287	
288	        func empty(_ missing: [SourceIdentifier]) -> RecipeReduction {
289	            RecipeReduction(values: [], totalGrams: totalGrams, componentGrams: componentGrams,
290	                            missingComponents: missing, unmeasuredNutrients: [],
291	                            conflictingUnits: [])
292	        }
293	        // An ingredient with no reference row contributes an unknown mass of
294	        // every nutrient. Totalling the rest would understate the dish across
295	        // the board, so nothing is computed and the gap is named instead.
296	        guard missing.isEmpty else { return empty(missing) }
297	        guard totalGrams > 0 else { return empty([]) }
298	
299	        // Every nutrient any ingredient mentions. One that only some mention is
300	        // still unmeasured below — an ingredient that does not list iron has
301	        // not thereby reported zero iron.
302	        var nutrientIDs: [String] = []
303	        var seen: Set<String> = []
304	        for entry in loaded {
305	            for value in entry.values where !seen.contains(value.nutrientID) {
306	                seen.insert(value.nutrientID)
307	                nutrientIDs.append(value.nutrientID)
308	            }
309	        }
310	
311	        var values: [NutrientValue] = []
312	        var unmeasured: [String] = []
313	        var conflicting: [String] = []
314	
315	        for nutrientID in nutrientIDs.sorted() {
316	            var total = 0.0
317	            var unit: String?
318	            var unitConflict = false
319	            var complete = true
320	
321	            for entry in loaded {
322	                guard let value = entry.values.first(where: { $0.nutrientID == nutrientID }),
323	                      let scaled = value.scaled(toGrams: entry.component.grams) else {
324	                    complete = false
325	                    break
326	                }
327	                // No unit is converted here, for the same reason `UnitRegistry`
328	                // converts none in Laboratory: a factor applied silently is a
329	                // wrong number nobody can see.
330	                if let unit, UnitRegistry.key(unit) != UnitRegistry.key(value.sourceUnit) {
331	                    unitConflict = true
332	                    break
333	                }
334	                unit = value.sourceUnit
335	                total += scaled
336	            }
337	
338	            if unitConflict { conflicting.append(nutrientID); continue }
339	            guard complete else { unmeasured.append(nutrientID); continue }
340	
341	            values.append(NutrientValue(
342	                foodRef: ref, nutrientID: nutrientID,
343	                amount: total / totalGrams * 100,
344	                qualifier: .calculatedRecipe,
345	                sourceValue: "sum of \(loaded.count) components over \(totalGrams) g",
346	                sourceNutrientID: nutrientID, sourceUnit: unit ?? "",
347	                licenceGroup: .permissive))
348	        }
349	
350	        return RecipeReduction(values: values, totalGrams: totalGrams,
351	                               componentGrams: componentGrams, missingComponents: [],
352	                               unmeasuredNutrients: unmeasured, conflictingUnits: conflicting)
353	    }
354	}

133	/// Persistence for the food log, and its timeline provider.
134	///
135	/// Holds what was eaten, not what it contained. Energy and nutrient totals are
136	/// a read-side join against the nutrition reference catalog: keeping them out
137	/// of here means a corrected reference value corrects every meal already
138	/// logged against it, instead of leaving thousands of frozen numbers behind.
139	public struct NutritionLogStore: TimelineProviding, @unchecked Sendable {
140	    public let domain = "nutrition"
141	    private let db: Database
142	    private let clock: any Clock
143	    private let zone: ZoneContext
144	
145	    public init(db: Database, clock: any Clock = SystemClock(),
146	                zone: ZoneContext = ZoneContext(TimeZone.current)) {
147	        self.db = db
148	        self.clock = clock
149	        self.zone = zone
150	    }
151	
152	    private var nowText: String { ISO8601DateFormatter().string(from: clock.now) }
153	
154	    private static func validate(grams: Double?) throws {
155	        guard let g = grams else { return }
156	        guard g.isFinite, g > 0 else { throw NutritionLogError.invalidGrams(g) }
157	    }
158	
159	    // MARK: Writing
160	
161	    /// Records a meal, or revises the one this source already sent.
162	    ///
163	    /// An entry carrying an `externalID` is identified by
164	    /// `(source_system, external_id)`: re-importing it revises the held entry
165	    /// rather than adding a second meal, and revives it if the source had
166	    /// previously withdrawn it. A manual entry has no external id and is
167	    /// always a new meal.
168	    ///
169	    /// The outcome describes what happened to the entry's *values*, so a
170	    /// re-import that revives a withdrawn entry without changing anything comes
171	    /// back `.unchanged`. A caller that needs to know the entry is live again
172	    /// reads `entry(id:)`; treating `.unchanged` as "nothing happened" would
173	    /// miss the revival.
174	    @discardableResult
175	    public func record(_ draft: NutritionLogDraft) throws -> NutritionLogOutcome {
176	        try NutritionLogStore.validate(grams: draft.grams)
177	        return try db.transaction { () throws -> NutritionLogOutcome in
178	            if let externalID = draft.externalID,
179	               let held = try loadRow(sourceSystem: draft.sourceSystem, externalID: externalID) {
180	                var edit = NutritionLogEdit()
181	                edit.actor = draft.sourceSystem
182	                edit.foodRef = .set(draft.foodRef)
183	                edit.foodNameText = draft.foodNameText.map { FieldEdit<String>.set($0) } ?? .clear
184	                edit.grams = draft.grams.map { FieldEdit<Double>.set($0) } ?? .clear
185	                edit.quantityText = draft.quantityText.map { FieldEdit<String>.set($0) } ?? .clear
186	                edit.eatenAt = .set(draft.eatenAt)
187	                let outcome = try applyEdit(to: held, edit)
188	                // A source re-sending an entry it had withdrawn is asserting it
189	                // again. Matches HealthSampleStore's revival on re-arrival.
190	                if held.isDeleted {
191	                    try db.run("UPDATE nutrition_log SET deleted_at = NULL WHERE id = ?;",
192	                               [.text(held.id)])
193	                }
194	                return outcome
195	            }
196	
197	            let id = UUID().uuidString
198	            try db.run("""
199	            INSERT INTO nutrition_log
200	                (id, source_system, external_id, food_ref, food_name_text, grams,
201	                 quantity_text, eaten_at, eaten_precision, eaten_tz_offset_minutes,
202	                 eaten_tz_id, recorded_at, recorded_tz_offset_minutes, deleted_at)
203	            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, NULL);
204	            """, [
205	                .text(id), .text(draft.sourceSystem),
206	                draft.externalID.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
207	                .text(draft.foodRef.description),
208	                draft.foodNameText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
209	                draft.grams.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
210	                draft.quantityText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
211	                draft.eatenAt.isKnown ? .text(draft.eatenAt.text) : .null,
212	                .text(draft.eatenAt.precision.rawValue),
213	                draft.eatenAt.zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null,
214	                draft.eatenAt.zone.identifier.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
215	                .text(nowText),
216	                zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null
217	            ])
218	            return .inserted(logID: id)
219	        }
220	    }
221	
222	    /// Corrects a held entry. Previous values move to
223	    /// `nutrition_log_revision` with the actor, the reason, and the list of
224	    /// fields touched — never an unrecorded in-place overwrite.
225	    @discardableResult
226	    public func update(id logID: String, _ edit: NutritionLogEdit) throws -> NutritionLogOutcome {
227	        if case .clear = edit.foodRef { throw NutritionLogError.foodRefRequired }
228	        guard let held = try loadRow(id: logID) else {
229	            throw NutritionLogError.entryNotFound(logID)
230	        }
231	        guard edit.touchesAnything else { return .unchanged(logID: logID) }
232	        return try db.transaction { try applyEdit(to: held, edit) }
233	    }
234	
235	    /// Soft delete. The entry stops counting and stops appearing on the
236	    /// timeline; it is not erased, so a mistaken delete is recoverable and an
237	    /// importer re-asserting the entry revives it.
238	    @discardableResult
239	    public func delete(id logID: String) throws -> Bool {
240	        try db.run("""
241	            UPDATE nutrition_log SET deleted_at = ? WHERE id = ? AND deleted_at IS NULL;
242	            """, [.text(nowText), .text(logID)]) == 1
243	    }
244	
245	    /// Writes the revision and the new row. Caller owns the transaction.
246	    private func applyEdit(to held: NutritionLogEntry,
247	                           _ edit: NutritionLogEdit) throws -> NutritionLogOutcome {
248	        let foodRef = edit.foodRef.resolve(held.foodRef, cleared: held.foodRef)
249	        let foodNameText = edit.foodNameText.resolve(held.foodNameText)
250	        let grams = edit.grams.resolve(held.grams)
251	        let quantityText = edit.quantityText.resolve(held.quantityText)
252	        let eatenAt = edit.eatenAt.resolve(held.eatenAt, cleared: .unknown)
253	        try NutritionLogStore.validate(grams: grams)
254	
255	        var changed: [String] = []
256	        if foodRef != held.foodRef { changed.append("food_ref") }
257	        if foodNameText != held.foodNameText { changed.append("food_name_text") }
258	        if grams != held.grams { changed.append("grams") }
259	        if quantityText != held.quantityText { changed.append("quantity_text") }
260	        if eatenAt != held.eatenAt { changed.append("eaten_at") }
261	        guard !changed.isEmpty else { return .unchanged(logID: held.id) }
262	
263	        let next = Int(try db.query("""
264	            SELECT COALESCE(MAX(revision_number), 0) AS n
265	            FROM nutrition_log_revision WHERE log_id = ?;
266	            """, [.text(held.id)]).first?.int("n") ?? 0) + 1
267	        let revisionID = UUID().uuidString
268	        try db.run("""
269	        INSERT INTO nutrition_log_revision
270	            (id, log_id, revision_number, food_ref, food_name_text, grams, quantity_text,
271	             eaten_at, eaten_precision, eaten_tz_offset_minutes, eaten_tz_id,
272	             changed_fields, actor, reason_text, recorded_at)
273	        VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?);
274	        """, [
275	            .text(revisionID), .text(held.id), .integer(Int64(next)),
276	            .text(held.foodRef.description),
277	            held.foodNameText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
278	            held.grams.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
279	            held.quantityText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
280	            held.eatenAt.isKnown ? .text(held.eatenAt.text) : .null,
281	            .text(held.eatenAt.precision.rawValue),
282	            held.eatenAt.zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null,
283	            held.eatenAt.zone.identifier.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
284	            .text(changed.joined(separator: ",")), .text(edit.actor),
285	            edit.reasonText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null, .text(nowText)
286	        ])
287	
288	        try db.run("""
289	        UPDATE nutrition_log SET
290	            food_ref = ?, food_name_text = ?, grams = ?, quantity_text = ?,
291	            eaten_at = ?, eaten_precision = ?, eaten_tz_offset_minutes = ?, eaten_tz_id = ?
292	        WHERE id = ?;
293	        """, [
294	            .text(foodRef.description),
295	            foodNameText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
296	            grams.map { SQLValue.real($0) } ?? .null,
297	            quantityText.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
298	            eatenAt.isKnown ? .text(eatenAt.text) : .null,
299	            .text(eatenAt.precision.rawValue),
300	            eatenAt.zone.offsetMinutes.map { SQLValue.integer(Int64($0)) } ?? .null,
301	            eatenAt.zone.identifier.map { SQLValue.text($0) } ?? .null,
302	            .text(held.id)
303	        ])
304	        return .revised(logID: held.id, revisionID: revisionID,
305	                        revisionNumber: next, changedFields: changed)
306	    }

378	    ///
379	    /// The domain-value counterpart of `entries(from:to:)`: the timeline gets

381	    /// needs to join on. Both go through `placed` so the two can never disagree
382	    /// about which meals fall in a range.
