388	    /// A log entry with the time the timeline would place it at.
389	    public struct PlacedLogEntry: Sendable, Hashable {
390	        public let entry: NutritionLogEntry
391	        public let occurrence: PartialDateTime
392	        public let basis: TimeBasis
393	        public let rangeFit: RangeFit
394	    }
395	
396	    private func liveRows() throws -> [Row] {
397	        try db.query("""
398	            SELECT \(NutritionLogStore.columns) FROM nutrition_log
399	            WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
400	            """)
401	    }
402	
403	    /// Placement is the eaten time, else when it was recorded. There is no
404	    /// `reported` basis: a meal has no report, and falling back to
405	    /// `recorded_at` is the same weaker claim Laboratory marks that way.
406	    /// Nil when the entry cannot belong to the range at all.
407	    private static func placed(_ row: Row, in range: DateRange) -> PlacedLogEntry? {
408	        guard let held = entry(from: row) else { return nil }
409	        let occurrence: PartialDateTime
410	        let basis: TimeBasis
411	        if held.eatenAt.isKnown {
412	            occurrence = held.eatenAt
413	            basis = .occurrence
414	        } else if let recorded = PartialDateTime(storedText: held.recordedAt,
415	                                                 precision: .instant) {
416	            occurrence = recorded
417	            basis = .recorded
418	        } else {
419	            return nil
420	        }
421	        guard let fit = occurrence.fit(in: range) else { return nil }
422	        return PlacedLogEntry(entry: held, occurrence: occurrence, basis: basis, rangeFit: fit)
423	    }

425	    // MARK: - TimelineProviding
426	
427	    public func entries(from: String, to: String) throws -> [TimelineEntry] {
428	        guard let range = DateRange(from: from, to: to) else { return [] }
429	        return try liveRows().compactMap { row in
430	            guard let placed = NutritionLogStore.placed(row, in: range) else { return nil }
431	            let held = placed.entry
432	
433	            let value: ValuePresentation
434	            if let grams = held.grams {
435	                value = .quantity(text: String(grams), unit: "g")
436	            } else {
437	                // Not zero. Nobody said how much, which is a different fact —
438	                // the same distinction NutrientQualifier draws for nutrients.
439	                value = .missing(reason: "amount not stated")
440	            }
441	            return TimelineEntry(
442	                domain: domain, kind: "food", recordTable: "nutrition_log",
443	                recordID: held.id, occurrence: placed.occurrence, basis: placed.basis,
444	                title: held.foodNameText ?? held.foodRef.description,
445	                detail: held.quantityText, value: value, lifecycle: nil,
446	                rangeFit: placed.rangeFit)
447	        }
448	    }

62	    public func loggedFoods(from: String, to: String) throws -> [LoggedFood] {
63	        let cache = Cache(catalog)
64	        return try log.logged(from: from, to: to).map { placed in
65	            let ref = placed.entry.foodRef
66	            let food = try cache.food(ref)
67	            var energy: EnergyEstimate?

130	    public func totals(from: String, to: String) throws -> NutritionTotals {
131	        let cache = Cache(catalog)
132	        var counted: [(ref: SourceIdentifier, grams: Double)] = []
133	        var withoutAmount: [String] = []
134	        var withoutReference: [SourceIdentifier] = []
135	        var incomplete: Set<String> = []
136	        var kcal = 0.0
137	        var bases: Set<EnergyEstimate.Basis> = []
138	
139	        for placed in try log.logged(from: from, to: to) {
140	            let entry = placed.entry
141	            guard let grams = entry.grams else {
142	                withoutAmount.append(entry.id)
143	                continue
144	            }
145	            guard try cache.food(entry.foodRef) != nil else {
146	                withoutReference.append(entry.foodRef)
147	                continue
148	            }
149	            counted.append((entry.foodRef, grams))
150	
151	            if let energy = EnergyEstimate.per100g(try cache.values(entry.foodRef))?
152	                .scaled(toGrams: grams) {
153	                kcal += energy.kcal
154	                bases.insert(energy.basis)
155	            } else {
156	                // This meal contributed calories nobody can put a number on, so
157	                // the running total understates and must say so.
158	                incomplete.insert(Nutrient.energyKcal)
159	            }
160	        }
161	
162	        var nutrientIDs: Set<String> = []
163	        for (ref, _) in counted {
164	            nutrientIDs.formUnion(try cache.values(ref).map(\.nutrientID))
165	        }
166	
167	        var totals: [String: Double] = [:]
168	        for nutrientID in nutrientIDs {
169	            var sum = 0.0
170	            var unit: String?
171	            var usable = true
172	            for (ref, grams) in counted {
173	                guard let value = try cache.values(ref)
174	                        .first(where: { $0.nutrientID == nutrientID }),
175	                      let scaled = value.scaled(toGrams: grams) else {
176	                    usable = false
177	                    break
178	                }
179	                // Nothing here converts units, so two meals reporting a
180	                // nutrient on different scales are not added together.
181	                if let unit, UnitRegistry.key(unit) != UnitRegistry.key(value.sourceUnit) {
182	                    usable = false
183	                    break
184	                }
185	                unit = value.sourceUnit
186	                sum += scaled
187	            }
188	            if usable { totals[nutrientID] = sum } else { incomplete.insert(nutrientID) }
189	        }
190	
191	        return NutritionTotals(
192	            kcal: kcal, energyBases: bases, nutrients: totals, mealsCounted: counted.count,
193	            mealsWithoutAmount: withoutAmount, mealsWithoutReference: withoutReference,
194	            incompleteNutrients: incomplete.sorted())
195	    }
196	}

3	/// Processing Design v0.1 §3 — namespace, never renumber.
4	///
5	/// `usda:1105904`, `ciqual:1000`, `cofid:13-145`, `afcd:F002258`.
6	/// An Almanac-internal integer key is a private detail that must never replace
7	/// the publisher's identifier. Namespacing keeps a food traceable to its
8	/// publisher, lets two sources sit side by side, and — the point that matters —
9	/// keeps "remove a whole source" a one-line delete when a rights holder says no.
10	public struct SourceIdentifier: Codable, Sendable, Hashable, CustomStringConvertible {
11	    public let namespace: Namespace
12	    public let localID: String
13	
14	    public enum Namespace: String, Codable, Sendable, CaseIterable, Hashable {
15	        case usda, ciqual, cofid, afcd, frida
16	        case openFoodFacts = "off"
17	        case sfda, wger, freeExerciseDB = "fedb", everkinetic, opentraining
18	        /// Rows Almanac owns outright. The only namespace Almanac may license
19	        /// independently.
20	        case almanac
21	
22	        public var licenceGroup: LicenceGroup {
23	            switch self {
24	            case .usda: return .permissive
25	            case .almanac: return .native
26	            case .ciqual, .cofid, .afcd, .frida: return .attribution
27	            case .openFoodFacts: return .shareAlike
28	            case .sfda: return .restricted
29	            // Exercise sources carry per-entry licences (wger admits ODbL as a
30	            // possible value). They are never classified at source level —
31	            // exercise rows must carry their own group column.
32	            case .wger, .freeExerciseDB, .everkinetic, .opentraining: return .restricted
33	            }
34	        }
35	    }
36	
37	    public init(namespace: Namespace, localID: String) {
38	        self.namespace = namespace
39	        self.localID = localID
40	    }
41	
42	    public var description: String { "\(namespace.rawValue):\(localID)" }
43	
44	    public init?(parsing text: String) {
45	        guard let sep = text.firstIndex(of: ":") else { return nil }
46	        let ns = String(text[text.startIndex..<sep])
47	        let rest = String(text[text.index(after: sep)...])
48	        guard let namespace = Namespace(rawValue: ns), !rest.isEmpty else { return nil }
49	        self.init(namespace: namespace, localID: rest)
50	    }
51	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Processing Design v0.1 §2.
4	///
5	/// A nutrient value is never a bare number. `Tr` (trace) and `N` (not analysed)
6	/// in CoFID are not zero; casting them to Double yields NaN, and writing 0 tells
7	/// a user their iron intake was zero when the truth is that nobody measured it.
8	/// Three distinct facts — reported zero, trace, unmeasured — that a Double
9	/// collapses into one.
10	public enum NutrientQualifier: String, Codable, Sendable, CaseIterable, Hashable {
11	    case measured
12	    case trace
13	    case notAnalysed = "not_analysed"
14	    case belowLOQ = "below_loq"
15	    case borrowed
16	    case calculatedRecipe = "calculated_recipe"
17	    case calculatedFactor = "calculated_factor"
18	    case zeroReported = "zero_reported"
19	
20	    /// True when the value has a defensible numeric reading. For `trace` that
21	    /// reading is "negligible": no source publishes a number for a trace, so its
22	    /// `amount` is nil, and arithmetic takes it as zero and says so
23	    /// (`EnergyEstimate.inputsTakenAsZero`). `notAnalysed` has no reading at all.
24	    public var hasQuantity: Bool { self != .notAnalysed }
25	
26	    /// True when the value is known rather than inferred or absent.
27	    /// The UI greys anything that is not `measured` or `zeroReported`.
28	    public var isDirectlyObserved: Bool {
29	        self == .measured || self == .zeroReported
30	    }
31	}
32	
33	/// The value model from Processing Design v0.1 §2, as a Swift type.
34	/// `sourceValue` is the reversibility guarantee: whatever the parser gets
35	/// wrong, the original cell is still here to re-derive from without going
36	/// back to `raw/`.
37	public struct NutrientValue: Codable, Sendable, Hashable {
38	    public let foodRef: SourceIdentifier
39	    public let nutrientID: String
40	    public let amount: Double?
41	    public let qualifier: NutrientQualifier
42	    public let confidence: String?
43	    public let sourceValue: String
44	    public let sourceNutrientID: String
45	    public let sourceUnit: String
46	    public let licenceGroup: LicenceGroup
47	    public let basis: NutritionBasis
48	
49	    public init(
50	        foodRef: SourceIdentifier,
51	        nutrientID: String,
52	        amount: Double?,
53	        qualifier: NutrientQualifier,
54	        confidence: String? = nil,
55	        sourceValue: String,
56	        sourceNutrientID: String,
57	        sourceUnit: String,
58	        licenceGroup: LicenceGroup,
59	        basis: NutritionBasis = .per100g
60	    ) {
61	        self.foodRef = foodRef
62	        self.nutrientID = nutrientID
63	        self.amount = amount
64	        self.qualifier = qualifier
65	        self.confidence = confidence
66	        self.sourceValue = sourceValue
67	        self.sourceNutrientID = sourceNutrientID
68	        self.sourceUnit = sourceUnit

1	import Foundation
2	
3	/// Whether two reported units may be compared — **not** a converter.
4	///
5	/// This slice performs no automatic conversion. Blanket permission to convert
6	/// "dimensionless" quantities was withdrawn: a percentage, a ratio and a titer
7	/// are all dimensionless and none of them is interchangeable with another.
8	/// So compatibility requires the same semantic dimension *and* a known scale
9	/// relationship, and even then the answer is a verdict, not a converted number.
10	public enum UnitDimension: String, Sendable, CaseIterable, Hashable {
11	    case massPerVolume, substancePerVolume, mass, volume
12	    case percentage, ratio, titer, activityPerVolume, cellsPerVolume
13	}
14	
15	public enum UnitCompatibility: Sendable, Hashable {
16	    /// Same dimension and same scale — directly comparable.
17	    case identical(UnitDimension)
18	    /// Same dimension, different scale. `factor` converts left to right, but
19	    /// this slice does not apply it.
20	    case sameDimensionDifferentScale(UnitDimension, factor: Double)
21	    /// Known to be different dimensions — never comparable without an
22	    /// analyte-specific factor that this slice does not hold.
23	    case differentDimension(UnitDimension, UnitDimension)
24	    /// One or both units are not in the table. Not an assertion of anything.
25	    case undetermined
26	}
27	
28	public enum UnitRegistry {
29	    /// Deliberately small and explicit. An unknown unit yields `.undetermined`
30	    /// rather than a guess, and adding one is a data change with a stated
31	    /// dimension and scale.
32	    static let table: [String: (dimension: UnitDimension, scale: Double)] = [
33	        "g/l":      (.massPerVolume, 1.0),
34	        "mg/dl":    (.massPerVolume, 0.01),
35	        "mg/l":     (.massPerVolume, 0.001),
36	        "ug/l":     (.massPerVolume, 0.000001),
37	        "ng/ml":    (.massPerVolume, 0.000001),
38	        "ug/dl":    (.massPerVolume, 0.00001),
39	        "ng/dl":    (.massPerVolume, 0.00000001),
40	        "pg/ml":    (.massPerVolume, 0.000000001),
41	        "mol/l":    (.substancePerVolume, 1.0),
42	        "mmol/l":   (.substancePerVolume, 0.001),
43	        "umol/l":   (.substancePerVolume, 0.000001),
44	        "nmol/l":   (.substancePerVolume, 0.000000001),
45	        "pmol/l":   (.substancePerVolume, 0.000000000001),
46	        "kg":       (.mass, 1.0),
47	        "g":        (.mass, 0.001),
48	        "lb":       (.mass, 0.45359237),
49	        "%":        (.percentage, 1.0),
50	        "percent":  (.percentage, 1.0),
51	        "ratio":    (.ratio, 1.0),
52	        "titer":    (.titer, 1.0),
53	        "u/l":      (.activityPerVolume, 1.0),
54	        "iu/l":     (.activityPerVolume, 1.0),
55	        "iu/ml":    (.activityPerVolume, 1000.0),
56	        "10^9/l":   (.cellsPerVolume, 1.0),
57	        "10^12/l":  (.cellsPerVolume, 1000.0)
58	    ]
59	
60	    static func key(_ unitText: String) -> String {
61	        unitText.lowercased()
62	            .replacingOccurrences(of: " ", with: "")
63	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "µ", with: "u")
64	            .replacingOccurrences(of: "μ", with: "u")
65	    }
66	
67	    public static func assess(_ a: String?, _ b: String?) -> UnitCompatibility {
68	        guard let a, let b,
69	              let left = table[key(a)], let right = table[key(b)] else { return .undetermined }
70	        guard left.dimension == right.dimension else {
71	            return .differentDimension(left.dimension, right.dimension)
72	        }
73	        if left.scale == right.scale { return .identical(left.dimension) }
74	        return .sameDimensionDifferentScale(left.dimension, factor: left.scale / right.scale)
75	    }
76	
77	    /// Whether two observations may be placed on one series without conversion.
78	    /// `sameDimensionDifferentScale` is false here on purpose: conversion is
79	    /// deferred, so a scaled pair is comparable only once conversion lands.
80	    public static func directlyComparable(_ a: String?, _ b: String?) -> Bool {
81	        if case .identical = assess(a, b) { return true }
82	        return false
83	    }
84	}

2	@testable import AlmanacCore
3	
4	/// Migration 008: the nutrition reference tables, module-prefixed per
5	/// docs/architecture/health-data-foundation.md §12.
6	final class NutritionReferenceTests: XCTestCase {
7	
8	    private func migrated() throws -> Database {
9	        let db = try Database.inMemory()
10	        try MigrationRunner(migrations: AlmanacMigrations.all).migrate(db)
11	        return db
12	    }
13	
14	    private func seedOneFood(_ db: Database) throws {
15	        try db.execute("""
16	        INSERT INTO nutrition_source (namespace, dataset_id, name, release, licence, licence_group, attribution, url)
17	        VALUES ('cofid', 'cofid_2021', 'CoFID 2021', '2021', 'Open Government Licence v3.0', 'B',
18	                'Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.',
19	                'https://www.gov.uk/');
20	        INSERT INTO nutrition_nutrient (nutrient_id, infoods_tag, name, unit, description)
21	        VALUES ('protein', 'PROCNT', 'Protein', 'g', '');
22	        INSERT INTO nutrition_food (food_ref, namespace, local_id, licence_group, food_group_code,
23	                                    food_group_name, source_record)
24	        VALUES ('cofid:13-145', 'cofid', '13-145', 'B', 'DG', 'Vegetables, general', 'fixture');
25	        """)
26	    }
27	
28	    private func insertValue(_ db: Database, amount: String, qualifier: String, cell: String,
29	                             ref: String = "cofid:13-145") throws {
30	        try db.execute("""
31	        INSERT INTO nutrition_value (food_ref, nutrient_id, basis, amount, qualifier, source_value,
32	                                     source_nutrient_id, source_unit, licence_group)
33	        VALUES ('\(ref)', 'protein', 'per_100g', \(amount), '\(qualifier)', '\(cell)', 'PROT', 'g', 'B');
34	        """)
35	    }
36	
37	    func testMigration008AddsModulePrefixedReferenceTables() throws {
38	        let db = try migrated()
39	        let tables = Set(try db.query("""
40	            SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name LIKE 'nutrition!_%' ESCAPE '!';
41	            """).compactMap { $0.string("name") })
42	        XCTAssertEqual(tables, ["nutrition_source", "nutrition_nutrient", "nutrition_food",
43	                                "nutrition_food_name", "nutrition_value", "nutrition_reference_import"])
44	        XCTAssertEqual(try MigrationRunner(migrations: AlmanacMigrations.all).applied(in: db).last?.version, 8)
45	    }
46	
47	    // Defence in depth: the database refuses what the bundle guard refuses, by any route.
48	    func testTheTablesRefuseRestrictedRowsAndCoercedTokens() throws {
49	        let db = try migrated()
50	        try seedOneFood(db)
51	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try db.execute("""
52	            INSERT INTO nutrition_source (namespace, dataset_id, name, release, licence, licence_group, attribution, url)
53	            VALUES ('sfda', 'sfda', 'SFDA', '2026', 'unclear', 'D', '', '');
54	            """), "a group D source")
55	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try db.execute("""
56	            INSERT INTO nutrition_food (food_ref, namespace, local_id, licence_group, food_group_code,
57	                                        food_group_name, source_record)
58	            VALUES ('cofid:x', 'cofid', 'x', 'C', '', '', '');
59	            """), "a group C food")
60	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try insertValue(db, amount: "0", qualifier: "trace", cell: "Tr"), "Tr coerced to 0")
61	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try insertValue(db, amount: "NULL", qualifier: "measured", cell: "2.9"))
62	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try insertValue(db, amount: "0.5", qualifier: "zero_reported", cell: "0.5"))
63	        XCTAssertThrowsError(try insertValue(db, amount: "2.9", qualifier: "guessed", cell: "2.9"))
64	        XCTAssertNoThrow(try insertValue(db, amount: "NULL", qualifier: "trace", cell: "Tr"))
65	    }
66	
67	    func testEveryQualifierTheSwiftEnumKnowsIsAccepted() throws {

import Foundation

public enum NutritionError: Error, CustomStringConvertible, Sendable {
    case foodNotFound(SourceIdentifier)
    case invalidGramWeight(Double)
    case invalidAmount(Double)
    case notANativeFood(SourceIdentifier)
    case recipeCycle(SourceIdentifier)
    case dishHasNoRecipe(SourceIdentifier)

    public var description: String {
        switch self {
        case .foodNotFound(let ref):
            return "no food '\(ref)' in the nutrition catalog."
        case .invalidGramWeight(let g):
            return "a portion's gram weight must be finite and greater than zero; got \(g)."
        case .invalidAmount(let a):
            return "a measure's amount must be finite and greater than zero; got \(a)."
        case .notANativeFood(let ref):
            return "'\(ref)' is published by \(ref.namespace.rawValue); only 'almanac:' foods "
                 + "may be authored here. A publisher's row is corrected upstream, not edited."
        case .recipeCycle(let ref):
            return "'\(ref)' would end up an ingredient of itself, directly or through "
                 + "another dish. The reduction would then compute each from the other's "
                 + "previous answer and report a number with nothing behind it."
        case .dishHasNoRecipe(let ref):
            return "'\(ref)' has no recipe to recompute from. Its values were entered "
                 + "directly, and reducing an empty ingredient list would replace them "
                 + "with nothing."
        }
    }
}

9	final class NutritionLogTests: XCTestCase {
10	
11	    private var path = ""
12	    private let clock = FixedClock(Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_500_000))  // 2026-03-14

16	        path = NSTemporaryDirectory() + "almanac-nutrition-\(UUID().uuidString).sqlite"
17	    }
18	
19	    override func tearDown() {
20	        for suffix in ["", "-wal", "-shm"] {
21	            try? FileManager.default.removeItem(atPath: path + suffix)
22	        }
23	        super.tearDown()
24	    }
25	
26	    private func open() throws -> (Database, NutritionLogStore) {
27	        let db = try Database(path: path)
28	        try MigrationRunner(migrations: AlmanacMigrations.all).migrate(db)
29	        return (db, NutritionLogStore(db: db, clock: clock,
30	                                      zone: ZoneContext(offsetMinutes: 180, identifier: "Asia/Riyadh")))
31	    }
32	
33	    private let rice = SourceIdentifier(namespace: .usda, localID: "1105904")
34	    private let bulgur = SourceIdentifier(namespace: .cofid, localID: "13-145")
35	
36	    private func lunch(_ grams: Double?) -> NutritionLogDraft {
37	        NutritionLogDraft(
38	            foodRef: rice, grams: grams,
39	            eatenAt: PartialDateTime(text: "2026-03-14T12:30:00+03:00", precision: .instant,
40	                                     zone: ZoneContext(offsetMinutes: 180, identifier: "Asia/Riyadh")),
41	            foodNameText: "Rice, white, cooked",
42	            quantityText: grams == nil ? nil : "1 cup")
43	    }
44	
45	    // MARK: - Writing and reading back
46	
47	    func testRecordsAMealAndReadsItBackFromDisk() throws {
48	        let logID: String
49	        do {
50	            let (_, log) = try open()
51	            let outcome = try log.record(lunch(150))
52	            guard case .inserted(let id) = outcome else {
53	                return XCTFail("expected an insert, got \(outcome)")
54	            }
55	            logID = id
56	        }
57	
58	        let (_, log) = try open()
59	        let held = try XCTUnwrap(try log.entry(id: logID))
60	        XCTAssertEqual(held.foodRef, rice)
61	        XCTAssertEqual(held.foodRef.description, "usda:1105904",
62	                       "the publisher's identifier survives the round trip, not an internal key")
63	        XCTAssertEqual(held.grams, 150)
64	        XCTAssertEqual(held.quantityText, "1 cup", "what the person typed is kept verbatim")
65	        XCTAssertEqual(held.eatenAt.precision, .instant)
66	        XCTAssertEqual(held.eatenAt.zone.identifier, "Asia/Riyadh",
67	                       "the zone the meal was eaten in is not normalised away")
68	        XCTAssertEqual(held.sourceSystem, "manual")

+    // MARK: - Arabic search folding
+    /// A food's `name_fold` is computed once, at import (`NutritionReferenceImporter`,
+    /// mirroring `TextFold.fold` exactly as it would run there), and stored —
+    /// these tests seed it the same way rather than through the importer, to
+    /// stay focused on `NutritionCatalog.search`'s own folded matching.
+    private func seedArabicFood(_ db: Database, ref: String, arabicName: String) throws {
+        try db.execute("""
+        INSERT INTO nutrition_source (namespace, dataset_id, name, release, licence, licence_group,
+                                      attribution, url)
+        VALUES ('almanac', 'almanac_native', 'Almanac native foods', '', 'Almanac proprietary', 'N', '', '')
+        ON CONFLICT (namespace) DO NOTHING;
+        let localID = String(ref.split(separator: ":", maxSplits: 1)[1])
+        try db.run("""
+            INSERT INTO nutrition_food (food_ref, namespace, local_id, licence_group, food_group_code,
+                                        food_group_name, source_record)
+            VALUES (?, 'almanac', ?, 'N', '', '', 'fixture');
+            """, [.text(ref), .text(localID)])
+        try db.run("""
+            INSERT INTO nutrition_food_name (food_ref, language, name, is_primary, name_fold)
+            """, [.text(ref), .text(arabicName), .text(TextFold.fold(arabicName))])
+    /// Hamza and harakat variants of one word must fold to the same key, and
+    /// tatweel (an elongation mark, never a letter) must be dropped rather
+    /// than treated as one.
+    func testSearchMatchesHamzaHarakatAndTatweelVariants() throws {
+        let db = try migrated()
+        // "إبريق" (a jug) written with an initial hamza-below, diacritics, and
+        // a tatweel inserted between the second and third letters.
+        try seedArabicFood(db, ref: "almanac:jug", arabicName: "إِبْرِيـــق")
+        let results = try NutritionCatalog(db: db).search("ابريق")
+        XCTAssertEqual(results.map(\.ref.description), ["almanac:jug"],
+                       "hamza, harakat and tatweel are decoration, not identity")
+    /// A measure or food name with irregular internal spacing still folds to

+    /// the typed query never breaks the match.
+    func testSearchFoldsArabicNamesAcrossSurroundingAndInternalSpaces() throws {

content.content:
# Almanac implementation status

Updated 2026-09-13. Work continues from `8836166` on `codex/manual-entry`; all
preceding commits are preserved. The nutrition work below is uncommitted in the
working tree. Nothing pushed.

## Verified core

Swift 6.3.3 on x86_64 Linux (`yamal`, `source env.sh`): **115 XCTest tests —
114 pass, 1 opt-in test skipped, zero failures.** Plain `swift build && swift
test`; the default parallel build works on this machine. The skipped test
imports the real bundle, and passes when enabled:

```sh
ALMANAC_NUTRITION_BUNDLE=~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite \
    swift test --filter NutritionRealBundleTests
```

Python 3.14, `tools/nutrition`: **101 unittest tests, zero failures**, including
the real-lake integration tests:

```sh
cd tools/nutrition && ALMANAC_NUTRITION_INTEGRATION=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```

Earlier records: 85 tests on Swift 6.0.3 in the 2026-09-08 session container
(`-j 1 -Xswiftc -disable-batch-mode`); 79 on Swift 6.3.3 per the user log. No
change has been run on an Apple platform.

## Nutrition module (2026-09-13)

The 2026-09-13 handoff's build order, steps 1–6:

1. Nutrient dictionary and qualifier vocabulary as data: `tools/nutrition/dictionary/`.
2. USDA Foundation Foods extracted, and 3. canonicalised (395 foods).
4. Bundle step with the failing licence assertion (`A`, `B`, `N` or the build
   fails), built while USDA was the only source.
5. CIQUAL 2025, CoFID 2021 and AFCD R3 extracted and canonicalised; union; the
   bundle holds 8,354 foods and 49,036 values. `qa` re-reads every mapped raw
   cell with independent readers: passed, 0 tokens coerced.
6. AlmanacCore: `LicenceGroup.native` (`N`, ships; the `almanac` namespace moved
   from `A` to `N`); `NutrientValue.basis`; migration 008 (`nutrition_*`
   reference tables with licence and qualifier CHECKs);
   `NutritionReferenceImporter` (re-runs the licence assertion against Swift's
   own registry before copying anything, in one transaction); `NutritionCatalog`
   (food, values, bases, calories, folded search); `GeneralAtwater` and
   `EnergyEstimate` (4/4/9/7 on total carbohydrate, publisher's figure as a
   labelled fallback).

Details: `docs/features/nutrition.md`. Pipeline contract:
`tools/nutrition/README.md`. Findings in the data:
`~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING-LOG-2026-09-13.md`.

Not done: Almanac-native dish data (blocked on Yazeed); wiring the bundle
import into the app target (needs the Apple toolchain); food logging and portions.

## Nutrition portions, pipeline side (2026-09-15)

`tools/nutrition/` step 1 of the 2026-09-14 handoff's build order: a fourth
canonical file (`portions.csv`) and bundle table (`nutrition_portion`)
carrying USDA `food_portion` (household measures) and CoFID "1.2 Factors"
(specific gravity, edible proportion). Details: `docs/features/nutrition.md`
§8; contract: `tools/nutrition/README.md` "Canonical format".

Python 3.14, `tools/nutrition`: **102 unittest tests, zero failures**,
including the real-lake integration tests and a new fidelity check
(`qa.portion_fidelity`) that re-reads every raw portion cell independently —
0 problems against the full 8,354-food lake (3,064 raw cells re-read: 123
household measures, 2,887 edible proportions, 54 specific gravities).

**Not reconciled with AlmanacCore.** A concurrent branch (uncommitted at the
time of writing) independently built its own `nutrition_portion` table
(migration 010) scoped to household measures only, with `edible_proportion`
living on a separate `nutrition_dish` table for the user's own `almanac:`
dishes — it has no slot for CoFID's per-reference-food edible proportion or
specific gravity. `NutritionReferenceImporter` was deliberately left
untouched here rather than risk clobbering that in-progress, uncommitted
work; the Swift test counts above predate it and were not re-verified this
session. See `docs/features/nutrition.md` §8 before starting that
reconciliation.

## Targeted corrections

- Unranked report imports default to `holdAsConflict`. Incoming report content
  is retained. `resolveReportConflict` accepts/rejects atomically, requiring an
  actor and reason and recording resolution time. Resolved proposals no longer
  count as unresolved, including replays of rejected equal-version content.
  Resolution fields are available through `reportRevisions`.
- Explicit observation corrections compare only with the current revision.
  A → B → deliberate A creates three attributable revision events. Import
  replay detection still searches historical fingerprints and creates no copy.
- Unchanged report content advances a newer source ordering marker. A/v1 →
  A/v3 → B/v2 retains A/v3. Conflicting equal versions are held for review.
  Overlapping partial issue dates do not establish ordering.
- Date-only strings have no textual offset. Time, calendar and offset syntax
  are validated. Unknown-offset local times remain unknown; timeline filtering
  conservatively widens the possible span and labels it potential.
- `saveManualEdit` commits value and metadata together. A failed metadata
  change rolls back the content revision too.

`RequestedFixTests` covers these regressions. Existing laboratory, import,
manual-entry, timeline, migration, catalog and synchronization tests also pass.
The earlier file-backed create/reopen/edit/history test remains in the suite.

## Schema and integrity

Migration 007 is appended; migrations 001–006 are unchanged. It removes the
unique observation fingerprint constraint (needed for deliberate reverts),
keeps the lookup index, and adds report-conflict resolution attribution.
Observation identity, revision numbering and the one-current-revision rule
remain intact. Catalog IDs and existing data are preserved.

The repository contains a reusable catalog, aliases, panels, reports,
observations with revisions, metadata correction history, module-provided
timeline queries, and the existing body-mass sample store. No additional
tracker or import automation was added.

The catalog coverage document remains the inventory of seeded and unseeded
tests. The catalog is not complete. Reference intervals remain result-specific;
no global intervals, medical interpretation or automatic conversion were added.

## Interface status

Native manual-entry code is authored in `Native/Almanac`, with an iOS 17+
Xcode app target and shared scheme in `Native/Almanac.xcodeproj`. It uses the
existing local `AlmanacCore` package.

Implemented screens: report list/create/edit/detail; result entry/editing with
canonical and alias search; longitudinal test history and source-report links;
separate content/metadata revision history; and report-conflict accept/reject.
Original units, source text, comparators, laboratory ranges, specimens and
unknown/partial dates remain visible and editable. Saving a correction requires
a reason and uses the atomic core edit API.

Linux Swift parsing passes for all four UI source files. Project references,
local package path and shared-scheme XML pass consistency checks. This does not
establish SwiftUI type correctness or a usable running Apple application.
See `Native/README.md` for the Apple build command and outstanding interactive
acceptance steps. No screenshots or runtime verification are claimed.

## Remaining boundaries

- Apple SDK compilation, Simulator launch and interactive UI verification have
  not been performed in this Linux environment.
- Document import and document-file backup/restore remain deferred. The SQLite
  snapshot does not include document files.
- The current storage model is a local personal database. There is no multi-user
  account boundary or server authorization layer; do not claim cross-user RLS.
- Timeline filtering still runs in Swift over current records.
- No automatic unit conversion, OCR, AI interpretation or new tracker.
- The separate Technical Spec / BRD is not present in this checkout.

To verify the modified core on yamal after importing this branch:

```sh
cd ~/projects/almanac
source env.sh
swift build
swift test
```

## 8. Portions (pipeline side, 2026-09-15)

`tools/nutrition/README.md` "Canonical format" and "Source rules" are the
contract; this is the summary. A fourth canonical file, `portions.csv`,
carries household-measure-to-gram conversion (Processing Design v0.1 §4),
validated independently of `values.csv` (`model.validate_portions`) so a
source with none is unaffected:

| Kind | Source | What it says |
|---|---|---|
| `household_measure` | USDA `food_portion` | `amount` of a named unit (e.g. "cup") weighs `value` grams |
| `specific_gravity` | CoFID "1.2 Factors" | the food's density, grams per mL |
| `edible_proportion` | CoFID "1.2 Factors" | the fraction of a gross weight that is edible |

The bundle's `nutrition_portion` table (schema v1, still version 1 — an
additive table) carries all three. QA (`portion_fidelity`) independently
re-reads USDA's `food_portion.csv` and CoFID's Factors sheet and compares
against canonical, the same discipline as the nutrient fidelity check; on the
full lake it re-reads 3,064 raw cells (123 household measures, 2,887 edible
proportions, 54 specific gravities) with 0 problems.

**Why nothing imports it yet.** AlmanacCore independently grew its own
`nutrition_portion` table (migration 010, uncommitted at the time this was
written) — household measures only, keyed differently, with
`edible_proportion` living on a separate `nutrition_dish` table scoped to the
user's own `almanac:` dishes. CoFID's `edible_proportion`/`specific_gravity`
are per **reference food** (thousands of CoFID foods, not just dishes), which
does not fit that slot. Reconciling the two schemas is unstarted; read both
migration files and this pipeline's `portions.csv` contract before doing it.

## Nutrition: transactions, portions, native dishes, the food log (2026-09-15)

The AlmanacCore side of the 2026-09-14 `claude/ponytail-anxf91` handoff,
reconciled onto `codex/manual-entry`'s bundle-imported schema (migration 008
wins over that branch's competing `nutrition_food`/`nutrition_value` — richer,
namespaced, per-basis, already populated with 8,354 real foods). Its own
migration 008 comment called this "a mechanical merge, but a real one"; in
practice the two schemas differed enough (namespace, basis, multi-language
names vs. a flat single-language table) that every ported file needed
rewriting against `NutritionCatalog`'s actual shape, not just repointing.

- **`Database.transaction` nests** (`Database.swift`): a call made while one is
  already open now uses a `SAVEPOINT` instead of failing, guarded by a
  per-connection `NSRecursiveLock` so a second thread mid-transaction gets a
  genuine outer transaction rather than silently attaching to the first
  thread's work. `DatabaseTests.swift`, 9 tests, ported unchanged — it never
  depended on the nutrition schema.
- **Migrations 009-011**: `nutrition_log`/`nutrition_log_revision` (009, the
  food log — untyped `food_ref`, no foreign key, so removing a reference
  source can never erase a meal); `nutrition_dish` + `nutrition_portion` +
  `nutrition_dish_component` (010); the portion-identity unique index (011).
  `nutrition_dish` holds `yield_grams`/`edible_proportion` for `almanac:`
  foods in its own table rather than widening migration 008's `nutrition_food`
  — that table intentionally mirrors the bundle schema, and a dish-only column
  would break the mirror. (§8 above names the still-open question these three
  tables don't answer: CoFID ships edible-proportion/specific-gravity for
  *every* reference food, not just dishes, and that doesn't fit here either.)
- **`NutritionDishEditor`** (`NutritionDish.swift`): create/edit/delete for
  `almanac:` foods; `setRecipe`/`recompute` with cycle detection and
  missing-ingredient/unmeasured-nutrient/unit-conflict reporting
  (`RecipeReduction`). Reduction always writes basis `.per100g` (a dish is
  solid) and `ref.namespace.licenceGroup` for the value rows — the source
  branch hardcoded licence group A there, which would have mislabelled every
  computed dish value.
- **`NutritionCatalog`** gained portion read/write (`addPortion`, `portion(of:
  unit:modifier:)`, `grams(of:...)`, English-plural matching, ambiguity
  returned rather than guessed) — ported as-is, schema-independent.
  `edibleGrams`/`removeSource` were not ported: the first needs the
  reference-food edible-proportion CoFID data §8 is about, the second is
  already subsumed by the importer fix below.
- **`NutritionLogStore`/`NutritionSummary`** (food log, revisions, timeline
  integration, day totals): ported with call sites adjusted to
  `values(for:basis:)`/`EnergyEstimate.preferred(from:basis:)` instead of the
  source branch's single-basis catalog. `EnergyEstimate.scaled(toGrams:)` and
  `NutrientValue.scaled(toGrams:)` (`NutritionScaling.swift`) needed adding —
  this codebase's `EnergyEstimate` had no scaling method yet.
- **Defect found and fixed: `NutritionReferenceImporter` blanket-deleted and
  reimported every table on every `importBundle` call.** The bundle already
  carries an `almanac` source row and, per the fixture, can carry `almanac:`
  food rows of its own — a curated native food is ordinary reference data,
  replaced on reimport like any other. A user-authored dish is not, and the
  blanket delete would have erased every dish on the next bundle update, with
  nothing to distinguish the two: both are `namespace = 'almanac'`. Fixed by
  scoping the delete to `food_ref NOT IN (SELECT food_ref FROM
  nutrition_dish)` — only `NutritionDishEditor.create` ever inserts a
  `nutrition_dish` row, so its presence is exactly "a person authored this
  here," regardless of namespace. `nutrition_source`/`nutrition_nutrient` are
  upserted row-by-row rather than replaced, because a preserved dish's values
  still reference both and SQLite enforces foreign keys per-statement, not at
  transaction end — deleting either out from under a surviving row fails
  immediately, even mid-transaction. (SQLite also refuses `ON CONFLICT` after
  an `INSERT ... SELECT`; only a `VALUES`-sourced insert accepts it, hence the
  per-row loop instead of a set-based upsert.)
  `NutritionBundleImportTests.testReimportingReplacesAndDropsARemovedSource`
  and a new `NutritionDishTests` case
  (`testReimportingTheBundlePreservesADeviceAuthoredDishAndReplacesABundleShippedOne`)
  cover both directions.
- **Arabic search-folding regression coverage** added to
  `NutritionReferenceTests.swift` (hamza/harakat/tatweel folding, internal and
  surrounding whitespace, Arabic-Indic digits) against `NutritionCatalog.search`
  — `TextFold` itself is unchanged and shared with Laboratory; these three
  tests just pin that `NutritionCatalog` exercises it the same way.

**Verified:** `swift build && swift test` on Swift 6.3.3 (`yamal`, `source
env.sh`) — 174 tests, 0 failures, 1 opt-in test skipped (unchanged from
before). Satisfies the ponytail handoff's outstanding item 3 ("test on
6.3.3"); its item 2 (populate the catalog) was already done independently on
this branch (8,354 foods); its item 1 (the schema duplication) is this
section.

**Still open, not attempted here** — flagged rather than guessed at, per the
existing rule that publicly accessible is not the same as reconciled:
1. Unifying `nutrition_portion` (this section) with the pipeline's
   three-kind portion table (§8) — needs that work to land first; both are
   uncommitted and it would be reconciling against a moving target.
2. `edibleGrams` and any specific-gravity lookup — blocked on the same thing.
3. The Saudi/Gulf native dish *data* — unchanged, still blocked on supply, not
   a build task; `NutritionDishEditor` can author dishes today, there just
   aren't any yet.
4. Portions/dish-components on a *non-native* reference food do not survive
   that food's own reimport (`ON DELETE CASCADE` from `nutrition_food`, which
   a bundle-namespace food is still fully replaced on) — pre-existing
   behaviour of the "replace on reimport" design, not introduced here, and
   out of scope for this pass.
5. A second, apparently unrelated concurrent session added hydration tracking
   (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Hydration/`, migration 012) to this same working tree
   while this work was in progress. No collision occurred — its migration
   number was claimed after this session's 009-011 — but it is a reminder this
   checkout had two sessions writing to it at once.

Updated 2026-09-13. Work continues from `8836166` on `codex/manual-entry`; all
preceding commits are preserved. The nutrition work below is uncommitted in the
working tree. Nothing pushed.

## Verified core

Swift 6.3.3 on x86_64 Linux (`yamal`, `source env.sh`): **115 XCTest tests —
114 pass, 1 opt-in test skipped, zero failures.** Plain `swift build && swift
test`; the default parallel build works on this machine. The skipped test
imports the real bundle, and passes when enabled:

```sh
ALMANAC_NUTRITION_BUNDLE=~/ALManac-food-data/build/almanac.sqlite \
    swift test --filter NutritionRealBundleTests
```

Python 3.14, `tools/nutrition`: **101 unittest tests, zero failures**, including
the real-lake integration tests:

```sh
cd tools/nutrition && ALMANAC_NUTRITION_INTEGRATION=1 python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .
```

Earlier records: 85 tests on Swift 6.0.3 in the 2026-09-08 session container
(`-j 1 -Xswiftc -disable-batch-mode`); 79 on Swift 6.3.3 per the user log. No
change has been run on an Apple platform.

## Nutrition module (2026-09-13)

The 2026-09-13 handoff's build order, steps 1–6:

1. Nutrient dictionary and qualifier vocabulary as data: `tools/nutrition/dictionary/`.
2. USDA Foundation Foods extracted, and 3. canonicalised (395 foods).
4. Bundle step with the failing licence assertion (`A`, `B`, `N` or the build
   fails), built while USDA was the only source.
5. CIQUAL 2025, CoFID 2021 and AFCD R3 extracted and canonicalised; union; the
   bundle holds 8,354 foods and 49,036 values. `qa` re-reads every mapped raw
   cell with independent readers: passed, 0 tokens coerced.
6. AlmanacCore: `LicenceGroup.native` (`N`, ships; the `almanac` namespace moved
   from `A` to `N`); `NutrientValue.basis`; migration 008 (`nutrition_*`
   reference tables with licence and qualifier CHECKs);
   `NutritionReferenceImporter` (re-runs the licence assertion against Swift's
   own registry before copying anything, in one transaction); `NutritionCatalog`
   (food, values, bases, calories, folded search); `GeneralAtwater` and
   `EnergyEstimate` (4/4/9/7 on total carbohydrate, publisher's figure as a
   labelled fallback).

Details: `docs/features/nutrition.md`. Pipeline contract:
`tools/nutrition/README.md`. Findings in the data:
`~/ALManac-food-data/PROCESSING-LOG-2026-09-13.md`.

Not done: Almanac-native dish data (blocked on Yazeed); wiring the bundle
import into the app target (needs the Apple toolchain); food logging and portions.

## Nutrition portions, pipeline side (2026-09-15)

`tools/nutrition/` step 1 of the 2026-09-14 handoff's build order: a fourth
canonical file (`portions.csv`) and bundle table (`nutrition_portion`)
carrying USDA `food_portion` (household measures) and CoFID "1.2 Factors"
(specific gravity, edible proportion). Details: `docs/features/nutrition.md`
§8; contract: `tools/nutrition/README.md` "Canonical format".

Python 3.14, `tools/nutrition`: **102 unittest tests, zero failures**,
including the real-lake integration tests and a new fidelity check
(`qa.portion_fidelity`) that re-reads every raw portion cell independently —
0 problems against the full 8,354-food lake (3,064 raw cells re-read: 123
household measures, 2,887 edible proportions, 54 specific gravities).

**Not reconciled with AlmanacCore.** A concurrent branch (uncommitted at the
time of writing) independently built its own `nutrition_portion` table
(migration 010) scoped to household measures only, with `edible_proportion`
living on a separate `nutrition_dish` table for the user's own `almanac:`
dishes — it has no slot for CoFID's per-reference-food edible proportion or
specific gravity. `NutritionReferenceImporter` was deliberately left
untouched here rather than risk clobbering that in-progress, uncommitted
work; the Swift test counts above predate it and were not re-verified this
session. See `docs/features/nutrition.md` §8 before starting that
reconciliation.

## Targeted corrections

- Unranked report imports default to `holdAsConflict`. Incoming report content
  is retained. `resolveReportConflict` accepts/rejects atomically, requiring an
  actor and reason and recording resolution time. Resolved proposals no longer
  count as unresolved, including replays of rejected equal-version content.
  Resolution fields are available through `reportRevisions`.
- Explicit observation corrections compare only with the current revision.
  A → B → deliberate A creates three attributable revision events. Import
  replay detection still searches historical fingerprints and creates no copy.
- Unchanged report content advances a newer source ordering marker. A/v1 →
  A/v3 → B/v2 retains A/v3. Conflicting equal versions are held for review.
  Overlapping partial issue dates do not establish ordering.
- Date-only strings have no textual offset. Time, calendar and offset syntax
  are validated. Unknown-offset local times remain unknown; timeline filtering
  conservatively widens the possible span and labels it potential.
- `saveManualEdit` commits value and metadata together. A failed metadata
  change rolls back the content revision too.

`RequestedFixTests` covers these regressions. Existing laboratory, import,
manual-entry, timeline, migration, catalog and synchronization tests also pass.
The earlier file-backed create/reopen/edit/history test remains in the suite.

## Schema and integrity

Migration 007 is appended; migrations 001–006 are unchanged. It removes the
unique observation fingerprint constraint (needed for deliberate reverts),
keeps the lookup index, and adds report-conflict resolution attribution.
Observation identity, revision numbering and the one-current-revision rule
remain intact. Catalog IDs and existing data are preserved.

The repository contains a reusable catalog, aliases, panels, reports,
observations with revisions, metadata correction history, module-provided
timeline queries, and the existing body-mass sample store. No additional
tracker or import automation was added.

The catalog coverage document remains the inventory of seeded and unseeded
tests. The catalog is not complete. Reference intervals remain result-specific;
no global intervals, medical interpretation or automatic conversion were added.

## Interface status

Native manual-entry code is authored in `Native/Almanac`, with an iOS 17+
Xcode app target and shared scheme in `Native/Almanac.xcodeproj`. It uses the
existing local `AlmanacCore` package.

Implemented screens: report list/create/edit/detail; result entry/editing with
canonical and alias search; longitudinal test history and source-report links;
separate content/metadata revision history; and report-conflict accept/reject.
Original units, source text, comparators, laboratory ranges, specimens and
unknown/partial dates remain visible and editable. Saving a correction requires
a reason and uses the atomic core edit API.

Linux Swift parsing passes for all four UI source files. Project references,
local package path and shared-scheme XML pass consistency checks. This does not
establish SwiftUI type correctness or a usable running Apple application.
See `Native/README.md` for the Apple build command and outstanding interactive
acceptance steps. No screenshots or runtime verification are claimed.

## Remaining boundaries

- Apple SDK compilation, Simulator launch and interactive UI verification have
  not been performed in this Linux environment.
- Document import and document-file backup/restore remain deferred. The SQLite
  snapshot does not include document files.
- The current storage model is a local personal database. There is no multi-user
  account boundary or server authorization layer; do not claim cross-user RLS.
- Timeline filtering still runs in Swift over current records.
- No automatic unit conversion, OCR, AI interpretation or new tracker.
- The separate Technical Spec / BRD is not present in this checkout.

To verify the modified core on yamal after importing this branch:

```sh
cd ~/projects/almanac
source env.sh
swift build
swift test
```

On 2026-09-15, while reconciling a nutrition-module handoff on `codex/manual-entry`, a second, unrelated session added hydration tracking (`Sources/AlmanacCore/Hydration/`, a new migration) to the *same* working directory mid-session — new files appeared, `Migrations.swift` gained an extra entry I hadn't written, and the full-package build briefly failed on code I hadn't touched. It resolved itself (the other session fixed its own error) without intervention.

Separately, `docs/implementation-status.md` and `docs/features/nutrition.md` are actively used as *cross-session handoff notes*: a concurrent session (Python pipeline / portions work) left an explicit "Not reconciled with AlmanacCore... see §8 before starting that reconciliation" note addressed to whoever picked up the Swift-side schema conflict — which was exactly what I was doing.

**Why this matters:** `git status` before starting confirms whether the tree is actually clean, but a session can land uncommitted changes *during* your own turn — re-check before assuming your last read of a shared doc/migration-list file is still current, especially right before editing it. Don't fix another session's unrelated broken code; note it and move on. Treat these docs as messages other sessions write to each other, not just status snapshots — read the newest dated section before starting reconciliation work, and add a new dated section rather than rewriting someone else's in-progress one.

**How to apply:** Before large concurrent-risk edits (migrations, shared docs), `git status` again immediately prior. When a doc file explicitly flags "not reconciled" or "see X before doing Y," treat it as a directive from another session, not decoration. Related: [[build-not-replan]], [[almanac-doc-locations]].

content.text:
All three of the handoff's unblocked items are done. Summary:

**Reconciled the `nutrition_food`/`nutrition_value` duplication** (item 1) by porting `claude/ponytail-anxf91`'s non-conflicting work onto `codex/manual-entry`'s richer, already-populated schema (8,354 foods won over the other branch's flatter one):
- [Database.swift](Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/Database.swift) — transactions now nest (SAVEPOINT + recursive lock), so composed writes (a recipe + its derived values) don't need manual flag-threading
- [Migration009](Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/Migration009.swift)/[010](Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/Migration010.swift)/[011](Sources/AlmanacCore/Persistence/Migration011.swift) — food log, household measures, native dishes, portion-identity
- [NutritionDish.swift](Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/NutritionDish.swift), [NutritionLogStore.swift](Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/NutritionLogStore.swift), [NutritionSummary.swift](Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/NutritionSummary.swift) — dish authoring/recipe reduction, the food log, day totals

Along the way I found and fixed a real defect: `NutritionReferenceImporter` blanket-deleted every table on each bundle reimport, which would have silently erased every user-authored dish the moment the app updated its data bundle. Fixed by using presence of a `nutrition_dish` row to tell a person's own dish apart from a curated native food the pipeline ships — [NutritionReferenceImporter.swift](Sources/AlmanacCore/Nutrition/NutritionReferenceImporter.swift).

**Item 2 (populate the catalog)** was already done independently on this branch (8,354 foods, confirmed still intact). **Item 3 (test on 6.3.3)** — this whole session ran on `yamal`'s 6.3.3 toolchain throughout.

Added 59 new tests (`DatabaseTests`, `NutritionDishTests`, `NutritionLogTests`, `NutritionPortionTests`, 3 Arabic-folding regressions). Full suite: **174/174 passing**, 1 opt-in skipped, verified clean before and after a concurrent session landed unrelated hydration-tracking work in the same tree mid-session (harmless collision — see [implementation-status.md](docs/implementation-status.md) for the note I left).

Documented everything — judgment calls, the importer defect, and what's still open — in [docs/implementation-status.md](docs/implementation-status.md) and [docs/features/nutrition.md](docs/features/nutrition.md) §9, without touching the concurrent session's own §8.

**Left open, flagged not guessed at:** unifying my `nutrition_portion` with the pipeline's newer three-kind portions table (household measure + CoFID specific-gravity + edible-proportion) is a real remaining task, but that Python-side work is itself mid-flight in this same tree — reconciling against a moving target isn't the move. Saudi/Gulf dish data is still blocked, unchanged.

Nothing committed or pushed — say the word if you want that done.
